front: How many officials can a game have for the field-crew, and under what condition? Rule 2 — Officials | Section 1: Designation of Officials | Article 1 – Field Officials
back: The number of officials per game may be from 1 to 7, as specified by the governing authority.

front: Which field officials may be designated, depending on the size of the crew? Rule 2 — Officials | Section 1: Designation of Officials | Article 1 – Field Officials
back: Field officials will be designated as follows (for various sizes of crews): Referee (R), Umpire (U), Back Umpire (BU), Back Judge (BJ), Down Judge (DJ), Line Judge (LJ), and Side Judge (SJ).

front: What standard determines the number of officials per game, and what document is referenced for detailed responsibilities and positioning? Rule 2 — Officials | Section 1: Designation of Officials | Article 3
back: The number of officials per game shall be in accordance with the recommendations of the local, provincial, or national officials’ associations; responsibilities, positioning, and mechanics are covered in the CFOA/Football Canada Officials’ Training Manual.

front: What is the requirement regarding any agreement among field officials about calling fouls? Rule 2 | Section 2: Jurisdiction and Duties | Article 1 – Responsibility
back: No agreement shall be made that would prevent the calling of any foul by any official against either team.

front: When must field officials report a player’s possible concussion, and through whom? Rule 2 | Section 2: Jurisdiction and Duties | Article 1 – Responsibility
back: When field officials recognize a player showing signs, symptoms, or behaviors consistent with a concussion (e.g., loss of consciousness, headache, dizziness, confusion, balance problems), they shall report their concerns through the Referee to the head coach or appropriate health-care professional.

front: What equipment must each field official have? Rule 2 | Section 2: Jurisdiction and Duties | Article 2 – Equipment
back: Each field official shall be equipped with a whistle and a “red” coloured marker.

front: What happens when a whistle is sounded while the ball is in play, and when should it not be sounded for injury? Rule 2 | Section 2: Jurisdiction and Duties | Article 3 – Stoppage of Play
back: Sounding a whistle when the ball is in play causes the ball to be ruled dead and stops the game; the whistle should not be sounded in the event of injury until the ball is dead.

front: If the marker is thrown to indicate an infraction, how long does play continue? Rule 2 | Section 2: Jurisdiction and Duties | Article 4 – Signal for Infraction
back: The throwing of the marker indicates an infraction, but play shall continue until the sounding of a whistle.

front: How does the Referee signal that time is “in” to start play? Rule 2 | Section 2: Jurisdiction and Duties | Article 5 – Signal to Play
back: The Referee shall sound the whistle to indicate the ball is ready for play, and shall signal that “time is in” by a downward sweep of the arm from the overhead position.

front: Who marks the out-of-bounds spot when the ball goes out of bounds, and when? Rule 2 | Section 2: Jurisdiction and Duties | Article 6 – Out-of-Bounds Marking
back: The nearest official should mark the out-of-bounds spot when the ball goes out of bounds.

front: What must all officials be familiar with regarding penalty calls? Rule 2 | Section 2: Jurisdiction and Duties | Article 7 – Penalty Signals
back: All officials should be familiar with the approved signals.

front: When does the official report a foul to the Referee, depending on whether the ball is dead or alive? Rule 2 | Section 2: Jurisdiction and Duties | Article 8 – Foul Called
back: The official shall report it to the Referee immediately if the ball is dead, or if the ball is alive, as soon as it is dead.

front: What does the Referee do immediately after a foul is called (before further foul reporting steps)? Rule 2 | Section 2: Jurisdiction and Duties | Article 8 – Foul Called
back: The Referee shall give a preliminary signal to indicate the nature of the foul.

front: After the foul has been reported to the Referee, what sequence of actions does the Referee complete? Rule 2 | Section 2: Jurisdiction and Duties | Article 9 – Foul Reporting
back: The Referee will indicate the number of the player who committed the foul, give the penalty signal, assess the penalty, and signal that the ball is again ready for play.

front: When the ball has been whistled dead, what spot must the appropriate official mark, and what does it determine? Rule 2 | Section 2: Jurisdiction and Duties | Article 10 – Forward Progress
back: When the ball has been whistled dead, the appropriate official shall mark the spot of forward progress of the ball, which will be the point of the subsequent play.

front: Who takes primary charge of the game, and what authority does the Referee have over other officials? Rule 2 — Officials | Section 3: Referee (R) | Article 1 – Responsibility
back: The Referee shall take primary charge of the game and guide/direct the other officials. The Referee may overrule any other official.

front: How does the Referee handle disputes, and how final are the Referee’s decisions? Rule 2 — Officials | Section 3: Referee (R) | Article 1 – Responsibility
back: The Referee shall apply the rules, assess penalties, and rule upon disputes or situations not covered by the rules. The Referee’s decision on any situation in the game is final.

front: Under what condition may the Referee remove a sideline official, and what must happen immediately afterward? Rule 2 — Officials | Section 3: Referee (R) | Article 1 – Responsibility
back: The Referee may have removed any of the sideline officials if the Referee considers it necessary, and immediately require the replacement of any official so removed.

front: When must the Referee test the game balls, and how final is the Referee’s decision about them? Rule 2 — Officials | Section 3: Referee (R) | Article 1 – Responsibility
back: The Referee shall test the game balls 30 minutes before the game, and the Referee’s decision is final as to the suitability of the balls.

front: What should the Referee do about irregularities in field markings or ground rules before the game? Rule 2 — Officials | Section 3: Referee (R) | Article 2 – Field Markings
back: The Referee shall report any irregularities in field markings, or ground rules, to the captains before the game, and review these with the other officials before the game.

front: When a foul is called, what two explanations must the Referee provide to the relevant captains? Rule 2 — Officials | Section 3: Referee (R) | Article 3 – Options
back: The Referee shall explain to the captains of either team any ruling made or penalty assessed. When a foul is called, the Referee shall explain to the non-offending captain the application of the penalty, or any option to which the captain is entitled if they refuse the penalty.

front: Who must the Referee coordinate with to keep the down count? Rule 2 — Officials | Section 3: Referee (R) | Article 4 – Count of Downs
back: The Referee shall keep count of the downs, subject to a check with the Down Judge.

front: What is the Referee’s role in communication between officials and team captains/coaches? Rule 2 — Officials | Section 3: Referee (R) | Article 5 – Communication
back: The Referee shall be the sole means of communication between the officials and the team captains or coaches.

front: How is the Referee notified when 3 minutes remain, and what notifications follow? Rule 2 — Officials | Section 3: Referee (R) | Article 6 – 3-Minute Warnings
back: The Referee shall be notified by the Down Judge or Line Judge when 3 minutes of play remains in each half. The Referee shall notify the captains, and the nearest official shall notify the coaches of each team.

front: How does the Referee indicate that playing time has ended in a period? Rule 2 — Officials | Section 3: Referee (R) | Article 7 – End of Period
back: The Referee shall indicate that playing time has ended in each period by sounding the whistle and signaling to the Timer.

front: What must the Referee do when 3 minutes remain in the half time interval? Rule 2 — Officials | Section 3: Referee (R) | Article 8 – End of Half Time Interval
back: The Referee shall have the captains of each team warned when 3 minutes remains in the half time interval.

front: Where should the Referee position relative to Team A, and what key responsibilities must they cover? Rule 2 — Officials | Section 3: Referee (R) | Article 9 – Positioning
back: The Referee shall take primary charge of Team A and take a position behind Team A. The Referee is responsible to determine if the ball is put into play legally, cover the action of the passer and the kicker and their opponents.

front: When a ball goes out of bounds in flight, what specific action is the Referee responsible for? Rule 2 — Officials | Section 3: Referee (R) | Article 9 – Positioning
back: The Referee shall be responsible for marking the out-of-bounds spot when a ball goes out of bounds in flight.

front: What two calls is the Referee responsible for regarding laterals and onside kick situations? Rule 2 — Officials | Section 3: Referee (R) | Article 9 – Positioning
back: The Referee shall rule on lateral passes behind the line of scrimmage, and the position of onside players in an “onside kick” situation.

front: What area of play and player actions does the Umpire have primary jurisdiction over? Rule 2 — Officials | Section 4: Umpire (U) | Article 1 – Responsibility
back: The Umpire has primary jurisdiction over the actions of players of both teams on the line of scrimmage.

front: Where must the Umpire position themselves relative to the defensive line of Team B? Rule 2 — Officials | Section 4: Umpire (U) | Article 1 – Responsibility
back: The Umpire shall take a position behind the defensive line of Team B.

front: What does the Umpire supervise regarding Team A’s eligible pass receivers and line backers? Rule 2 — Officials | Section 4: Umpire (U) | Article 2 – Duties
back: The Umpire shall supervise the line backers and their use of hands on eligible pass receivers of Team A.

front: What passes and kicks does the Umpire cover, and over what line area? Rule 2 — Officials | Section 4: Umpire (U) | Article 2 – Duties
back: The Umpire shall cover short forward passes and short kicks over the centre of the line.

front: Under what condition does the Umpire check Team A’s ineligible receivers on the line of scrimmage? Rule 2 — Officials | Section 4: Umpire (U) | Article 2 – Duties
back: The Umpire checks that Team A ineligible receivers on the line of scrimmage do not proceed downfield before a forward pass is thrown (Exception 6.4.5.).

front: How does the Umpire assist with crack-back blocking, and where is that restricted area? Rule 2 — Officials | Section 4: Umpire (U) | Article 2 – Duties
back: The Umpire shall assist in coverage of crack-back blocking in the restricted area.

front: What jurisdiction does the Back Umpire have over player actions? Rule 2 | Section 5: Back Umpire (BU) | Article 1 – Responsibility
back: The Back Umpire has primary jurisdiction over the actions of players of both teams behind the Team B line.

front: Where must the Back Umpire position himself relative to Team B players? Rule 2 | Section 5: Back Umpire (BU) | Article 1 – Responsibility
back: He shall take a position behind the deepest Team B player.

front: What passes and kicks is the Back Umpire responsible for covering? Rule 2 | Section 5: Back Umpire (BU) | Article 2 – Duties
back: He covers long passes in the centre of the field and kicks downfield.

front: Under what condition does the Back Umpire rule field goal attempts, and from what range? Rule 2 | Section 5: Back Umpire (BU) | Article 2 – Duties
back: He rules field goal attempts from outside the 10 yard (metre) line, whether successful or not.

front: What duties are assigned to the Back Judge compared with another official? Rule 2 | Section 6: Back Judge (BJ) | Article 1
back: The duties of the Back Judge shall be identical with those of the Back Umpire.

front: What is the Down Judge primarily responsible for covering when the ball is snapped? Rule 2 — Officials | Section 7: Down Judge (DJ) | Article 1 – Responsibility
back: Primarily covering crack-back blocking by players positioned on their side of the field when the ball is snapped.

front: Where should the Down Judge take position relative to the sideline and which equipment, when setting up at the line of scrimmage? Rule 2 — Officials | Section 7: Down Judge (DJ) | Article 1 – Responsibility
back: On the line of scrimmage at a suitable distance in from the sideline on the same side of the field as the distance chain and Downsbox.

front: When should the Down Judge cover passes and kicks, and in what direction? Rule 2 — Officials | Section 7: Down Judge (DJ) | Article 2 – Passes and Kicks
back: When appropriate, cover passes down his/her side of the field and cover kicks down his/her side of the field.

front: What must the Down Judge do regarding substitutes, and what must be checked? Rule 2 — Officials | Section 7: Down Judge (DJ) | Article 3 – Substitutes; 3- and 1-Minute Warning
back: Systematically check his/her sideline for substitutes and ensure legality of substitution procedures.

front: When the timekeeper notifies the Down Judge, at what times must the Down Judge notify the Referee? Rule 2 — Officials | Section 7: Down Judge (DJ) | Article 3 – Substitutes; 3- and 1-Minute Warning
back: When 3 minutes remain in each half, and when 1 minute remains in each period.

front: How does the Down Judge assist with the distance chain and Downsbox placement? Rule 2 — Officials | Section 7: Down Judge (DJ) | Article 4 – Control of Minor Officials
back: Supervise the Yardstick officials and the Dowbox official in the placement of the distance chain and Downsbox, under the direction of the Referee.

front: What must the Down Judge do at the end of the 1st and 3rd periods regarding the distance chain? Rule 2 — Officials | Section 7: Down Judge (DJ) | Article 4 – Control of Minor Officials
back: Change the position of the distance chain at the end of the 1st and 3rd periods to the identical spot, at the opposite end of the field, corresponding to the point at which play ended in that period.

front: When the Referee requires a measure, what spot must the Down Judge mark on the chain and what must the Yardstick Official do? Rule 2 — Officials | Section 7: Down Judge (DJ) | Article 4 – Control of Minor Officials
back: Mark on the chain the spot corresponding to the farthest-from-the-ball cross-stripe farthest from the ball within the span of the distance chain, and have the Yardstick Official bring the distance chain to the Referee.

front: What must the Down Judge check after a penalty regarding distance? Rule 2 — Officials | Section 7: Down Judge (DJ) | Article 4 – Control of Minor Officials
back: Check distance applied on penalties.

front: What are the Line Judge’s duties, and how do they compare to the Down Judge’s duties? Rule 2 | Section 8: Line Judge (LJ) | Article 1 – Responsibility
back: The duties of the Line Judge shall be identical to those of the Down Judge covered in Section 7, Articles 1 to 3 inclusive, only.

front: Where is the Side Judge positioned relative to the sideline and the line of scrimmage? Rule 2 | Section 9: Side Judge (SJ) | Article 1 – Responsibility
back: The Side Judge is positioned on or near the sideline approximately eighteen to twenty yards in advance of the line of scrimmage.

front: Which side of the field does the Side Judge work on? Rule 2 | Section 9: Side Judge (SJ) | Article 1 – Responsibility
back: The Side Judge will work the same side of the field as the Down Judge.

front: Under whose direction must the Downbox and Yardstick Officials act, and where must the Downsbox and distance chain be positioned? Rule 2 — Officials | Section 10: Downbox and Yardstick Officials | Article 1 – Control
back: They shall act under the direction of the Down Judge. The Downsbox and distance chain shall be positioned out of bounds.

front: What must the Downbox Official do with the Downsbox before the ball is ready to be scrimmaged, and what must be indicated on it? Rule 2 — Officials | Section 10: Downbox and Yardstick Officials | Article 2 – Downsbox Position
back: The Downbox Official shall place the Downsbox at the point where the ball is to be scrimmaged, and indicate the number of each down on the Downsbox.

front: How are the two Yardstick Officials required to position the distance chain? Rule 2 — Officials | Section 10: Downbox and Yardstick Officials | Article 3 – Distance Chain Position
back: The two Yardstick Officials shall place the distance chain as directed by the Down Judge.

front: If a 3rd Yardstick Official is used on the sideline opposite the 10 yard (10 metre) objective line, what is the condition for using that marker rod, and what can be recorded? Rule 2 — Officials | Section 10: Downbox and Yardstick Officials | Article 4 – 3rd Yardstick Official
back: This marker will not be used to determine whether a first down has been gained. Under the direction of the Referee, penalties may be recorded.

front: What information must the Scorer receive before the game, and what must happen with the scoresheet after the game? Rule 2 — Officials | Section 11: Timekeeper and Scorer | Article 1 – Scoresheet
back: Prior to the game, the Scorer shall be provided with a complete list of the eligible competing players, including names and correct numbers. The score shall be kept as given by one of the field officials, and the scoresheet presented to the Referee after the game for signature.

front: How should the Timekeeper(s) keep time, especially when two timekeepers are appointed? Rule 2 — Officials | Section 11: Timekeeper and Scorer | Article 2 – Timekeeper’s Responsibility
back: The Timekeeper (or Timekeepers) shall keep time according to Rule 1 Section 5, following the recognized signals by the officials. If 2 timekeepers are appointed, they shall use one timing device placed between them and operated solely by one of them.

front: What must the Timekeeper do if the two timekeepers disagree? Rule 2 — Officials | Section 11: Timekeeper and Scorer | Article 2 – Timekeeper’s Responsibility
back: In the event of disagreement, the Referee shall be called immediately to settle any dispute or make any necessary adjustment.

front: When must the Timekeeper notify the Down Judge or Line Judge? Rule 2 — Officials | Section 11: Timekeeper and Scorer | Article 3 – 3-Minute Warning
back: The Timekeeper shall notify the Down Judge or the Line Judge when 3 minutes remain in the 2nd and 4th periods, and when 1 minute remains in each period.

front: What is the Last Minute Procedure at the start and end of the last minute of each period? Rule 2 — Officials | Section 11: Timekeeper and Scorer | Article 4 – Last Minute Procedure
back: Just prior to and during the last minute of play in each period, the Timekeeper takes a position on the sideline clearly visible to the officials. At the commencement of the last minute of play, the Timekeeper raises the flag and continues to keep it raised until the Timekeeper’s watch registers full time for the period; the flag is then immediately lowered so it is no longer visible to the officials.

front: Under what condition will play be put into play again if the ball becomes dead during the last minute and the flag is still raised? Rule 2 — Officials | Section 11: Timekeeper and Scorer | Article 4 – Last Minute Procedure
back: If the ball becomes dead on any play, and the flag is still raised, the ball will again be put into play.

front: What happens if the ball becomes dead and the flag has been lowered since the last time the ball was put into play? Rule 2 — Officials | Section 11: Timekeeper and Scorer | Article 4 – Last Minute Procedure
back: If the flag has been lowered since the last time the ball was put into play, the period will be over, and so declared by the Referee, subject to fouls committed during the last play.

front: How many points is a touchdown worth in this scoring table? Rule 3 — Scoring | Section 1: Table of Scores | Article 1
back: Touchdown = 6 points.

front: How many points is a field goal worth, and how does it differ from a convert? Rule 3 — Scoring | Section 1: Table of Scores | Article 1
back: Field Goal = 3 points; Convert = 1 or 2 points.

front: Under what condition is a team declared the winner? Rule 3 — Scoring | Section 1: Table of Scores | Article 1
back: The team scoring the majority of the points shall be the winner.

front: When is a touchdown scored based on the ball reaching the opponent’s goal line (including being in the air)? Rule 3 — Scoring | Section 2: Definitions | Article 1 – Touchdown
back: A touchdown is scored when the ball is in the opponent’s end zone in possession of a player, or when the ball in possession crosses or touches the goal line or the plane of the goal line, even in the air.

front: What happens to a touchdown if the ball is fumbled afterward or the player is forced back into the field of play? Rule 3 — Scoring | Section 2: Definitions | Article 1 – Touchdown
back: If, after a touchdown, the ball is fumbled or the player in possession is forced back into the field of play, the touchdown shall still score.

front: What is required for a field goal to score, including the key conditions after the kick? Rule 3 — Scoring | Section 2: Definitions | Article 2 – Field Goal
back: A field goal is scored by a drop or place kick (except on a kick off) when the ball, after being kicked and without again touching the ground, goes over the crossbar and between the goal posts (or goal posts produced) of the opponent’s goal, regardless of whether it touches the goal post assembly.

front: When does a field goal still score if the kicked ball touches or is touched before/after the line of scrimmage? Rule 3 — Scoring | Section 2: Definitions | Article 2 – Field Goal
back: If, after being kicked, the ball touches/is touched by any player before it crosses the line of scrimmage, or touches/is touched by a B player after it crosses the line of scrimmage, and the ball continues forward in the air over the crossbar between the goal posts, the field goal shall score.

front: Under what conditions is a safety touch scored (including kicks and blocked kicks)? Rule 3 — Scoring | Section 2: Definitions | Article 3 – Safety Touch
back: A safety touch is scored when the ball becomes dead in possession of a team in its own end zone, or goes out of bounds in the end zone, as a result of the ball being carried, kicked, fumbled, or otherwise directed from the field of play into the end zone by the team scored against, or as a DIRECT result of a kick being blocked in the field of play.

front: When can an interception in the field of play count as possession gained in the end zone? Rule 3 — Scoring | Section 2: Definitions | Article 3 – Safety Touch
back: If a player intercepts a forward pass in the field of play while moving toward the player’s goal line, and the official judges that the momentum carries the player into the player’s end zone, possession is deemed to have been gained in the end zone.

front: What must occur for a rouge to be scored (including possession after a kicked ball)? Rule 3 — Scoring | Section 2: Definitions | Article 4 – Rouge or Single Point
back: A rouge is scored when the ball becomes dead in possession of a team in its own end zone, or goes out of bounds in its end zone, because the ball was kicked into the end zone by an opponent; if a player catches a kicked ball in the field of play while moving toward their goal line and officials judge momentum carries them into their team’s end zone, possession is deemed to have been gained in the end zone.

front: On a kickoff, what condition must be met for the kicking team to score a rouge? Rule 3 — Scoring | Section 2: Definitions | Article 4 – Rouge or Single Point
back: For the kicking team to score a rouge on a kick off, the ball must touch the ground, a player, or an official, in bounds, after the ball has been kicked.

front: What happens if the ball is kicked directly out of bounds (in flight in the end zone) on a kickoff? Rule 3 — Scoring | Section 2: Definitions | Article 4 – Rouge or Single Point
back: If the ball is kicked directly out of bounds, in flight in the end zone, no point is awarded, and the ball will be scrimmaged by the receiving team at 1D on their own 20 yard (20 metre) line, at any point on or between the hash marks.

front: From where can a team attempt a convert after scoring a touchdown, and what is the minimum/maximum location limit mentioned? Rule 3 — Scoring | Section 2: Definitions | Article 5 – Convert
back: A team scoring a touchdown may attempt to add to its score by one scrimmage play at any point on or between the hash marks, or play from any point on or outside the opponent’s 5 yard (5 metre) line, within the hash marks. No convert attempt shall be made from within the 1 yard (1 metre) line.

front: What point values are available on a convert attempt, and what scoring/playing restrictions apply to each? Rule 3 — Scoring | Section 2: Definitions | Article 5 – Convert
back: A 1-point convert is by kicking a field goal. If the kick is unsuccessful, the ball is dead immediately. A 2-point convert is by scoring a touchdown; a punt or onside kick is prohibited, and if B gains possession, the ball is dead immediately.
